sections.tool_refs:
<tool_refs>
- Every tool result ends with `[tool-ref #N]`, its handle. A codemode script's result gets one handle; the calls inside the script get none.
- Cite evidence by handle instead of copying output. When you give the user results, a summary or a conclusion, cite the results behind each claim inline, e.g. `the build fails on missing headers (#12)` or `(#12, #14)`.
- Cite the result that first produced the evidence, not a later lookup or script that only re-shows it.
- To see earlier results again, use `tool_ref_get` (with `lines` for a range) instead of re-running the command. To find earlier calls, e.g. after context was summarized, use `tool_ref_grep`.
- In a codemode script both return data instead of text: the whole output and whole matching lines.
- Start every codemode script with a `// intent: <what it does and why, one line>` comment (after the `// @options:` line if there is one); it is shown to the user as the call's title.
</tool_refs>

with two extensions and writes report.json. TypeScript on Node 26, no runtime dependencies
outside the bundles.
</project>

sections.agents_md:
<agents_md>
path: /Users/retro9/Project/agents-infra/AGENTS.md
# agents-infra

Parent folder for all my agent infrastructure projects. Each subfolder is an independent project with its own repo, tooling, and conventions.

- `pi-agent/` – extensions, skills, and prompts for the pi coding agent (TypeScript)
- `jarvis-core/` – core agent system (Go)
- `agent-system-survey/` – research notes, design docs, and spikes (OpenShell, sandboxing, agent runners)

When working in a subproject, follow that project's own README/AGENTS.md.

# Branch Naming

- Branch name is `<type>/<name>` with a conventional type (`feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `ci`, ...), e.g. `fix/login`
- All repos in this folder are self-developed, personal project. You can create a feature branch and a worktree for a specific feature / task.
  After you finish a task, merge back to main branch directly. Don't open a merge request unless explictly told.

# Commiting Changes

- Message style should follow git conventional style strictly
</agents_md>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: codemode

variants.openai_lark:
start: options_source | plain_source
options_source: OPTIONS_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

OPTIONS_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @options:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

toolsAdded.name: worktree_add
toolsAdded.description: Create a git worktree for a branch in the worktree folder (<folder>/<repo>-wt/<branch with / as ->). Checks out the local branch if it exists, else tracks a remote branch of that name, else creates the branch from base. With enter: true, also enters it (see worktree_enter).

repo.description: Repository folder (relative to the session's working directory, or absolute). Default: the entered worktree's repository, else the one the working directory is in.

base.description: Start point of a new branch. Default: HEAD of the repository's main checkout

enter.description: Also enter the new worktree (like worktree_enter)

toolsAdded.name: worktree_enter
toolsAdded.description: Enter an existing worktree (by branch) for the rest of the session: relative paths of read/write/edit/ls/grep/find and every bash command run there, and write/edit outside it are blocked. Only the user can leave it.

repo.description: Repository folder (relative to the session's working directory, or absolute). Default: the entered worktree's repository, else the one the working directory is in.

toolsAdded.name: worktree_remove
toolsAdded.description: Remove the worktree of a branch. Keeps the branch; fails when the worktree has uncommitted changes or the session is in it.

repo.description: Repository folder (relative to the session's working directory, or absolute). Default: the entered worktree's repository, else the one the working directory is in.

toolsAdded.name: worktree_list
toolsAdded.description: List the worktrees of every repository in the workspace; * marks the one the session works in.

toolsAdded.name: send_to_leader
toolsAdded.description: Send the result of your task to the leader that started you. Call it exactly once, when you are done; the leader cannot answer questions.

status.description: "ok" when the task is done, "error" when you could not do it

summary.description: The outcome in a few sentences; the leader reads it first

detail.description: Structured result; must follow the result format given in the task

toolsAdded.name: tool_ref_get
toolsAdded.description: Show earlier tool results by their handle (the N of `[tool-ref #N]`): output, input or both. Output lines are numbered; use `lines` for a range and `maxChars` to see more.

lines.description: Output line range, 1-based and inclusive, e.g. [1, 80]; negative counts from the end, e.g. [-50, -1]

toolsAdded.name: tool_ref_grep
toolsAdded.description: Find earlier tool calls by regex over their input and output, newest first, with line numbers for tool_ref_get. `pattern: ".", in: "input"` lists the calls.

pattern.description: JavaScript regex, matched line by line; case-insensitive unless it has an uppercase letter

errors.description: true: only failed calls; false: only successful ones

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 0)
